one_liner: Help Scout has a broad OAuth2 REST Inbox API and an official MCP server, but API access requires a paid plan (Standard or above); the Free plan has none.
auth_notes: The fetched pages don't include the authentication docs. They do show that apps are created under My Apps with an App ID and secret, and that the MCP connector uses an OAuth login. The Docs API has its own API key. OAuth2 for the Inbox API, and the Basic-auth form of the Docs key, come from the draft and Composio's catalog (OAUTH2) and are not confirmed on the fetched pages.
access_notes: Help Scout's help article says each paid plan has different levels of API access, and the Free plan has none. Standard has no reporting endpoints. Plus and Pro have all endpoints. The homepage says "try Help Scout free", which suggests a trial may exist. The pages don't say whether the API works during a trial, so I couldn't confirm that.
blocker_notes: Testing the API needs a paid Help Scout plan (Standard or above). Reporting endpoints need Plus or Pro. The pages don't confirm whether a trial gives API access.

evidence.quote: The Free plan does not include access to the API or integrations.
Each paid Help Scout plan has different levels of API access.
Your Help Scout account must have API access, which is included on the Standard, Plus, and Pro plans.
Help Scout MCP gives AI assistants secure, official access to Help Scout data.
Set the remote MCP server URL to `https://mcp.helpscout.net/mcp`
Enabling Docs tools requires an additional step because the Docs API uses its own API key.
Don't enter a Help Scout App ID or secret from My Apps here; those are for the Help Scout API and won't work for the connector.
[Inbox API](https://developer.helpscout.com/mailbox-api/) - read and write data to Help Scout inboxes
[Webhooks](https://developer.helpscout.com/webhooks/) - get notified about activity in Help Scout
